description: April 2 birthday meaning: Aries decan 2, birthday number 2, Life Path by year, Chinese zodiac note and famous birthdays.
answer: In Western astrology, an April 2 birthday falls in Aries, in the second decan, with Mars as the sign's ruler and Sun as the decan's. In numerology the day gives birthday number 2. The Life Path also uses the birth year. Aries is cardinal and fire.

sections.heading: April 2 zodiac sign and personality
paragraphs: Two softens Aries without dimming it. On April 2 the Sun stands about twelve degrees into the cardinal fire sign, and Leo's ruler, the Sun, colours this decan with warmth. The reading is a generous, partnership-minded fighter who prefers to win alongside others and tends to bring out loyalty in a team.

On April 2 the Sun usually sits at about 12° Aries, in the second decan, where Sun is the sub-ruler alongside Mars. Between 10 and 19 degrees of Aries the Sun takes over as sub-ruler, lending this middle decan some of Leo's warmth and sense of occasion. The Martian drive is still there, yet it is often aimed at something worth being seen for: a cause, a team, a creative project with their name on it. Traditional writers associate this stretch with pride in the good sense, a wish to lead by example rather than by force. Generosity tends to come easily, and so can a sensitivity to being overlooked. A useful question for these Aries natives is whose applause actually matters, since chasing everyone's can scatter a strong fire.

sections.heading: April 2 in numerology
paragraphs: A birthday on the 2nd gives a birthday number of 2, unreduced and simple. Numerologists treat the day of birth as a secondary influence, a natural skill that colours the main Life Path without overriding it. The 2 is the number of the pair, so it is traditionally linked with tact, sensitivity and an instinct for what other people need. Someone born on this day may be the quiet mediator in a group, noticing tension long before it surfaces. The challenge often described for 2s is voicing their own view rather than adjusting it to keep the peace.

The Life Path, the main number in a numerology chart, also uses the birth year, so it changes from one April 2 birthday to the next: it is 4 for 1960, 5 for 1970, 6 for 1980 and 7 for 1990, for example. Some birth years on this date reach the master number 11.

sections.heading: Born on April 2: season, famous birthdays and Chinese zodiac
paragraphs: April birthdays arrive in full northern spring, with lengthening days and fast growth; in the southern hemisphere the month belongs to mid-autumn and harvest. Aries carries most of April, handing over to Taurus around April 19 or 20. As month 4, April brings numerology's number of structure, steadiness and hard work, a grounding counterweight to the quick fire of the month's early birthdays. April 2 is the 92nd day of the year (93rd in a leap year). By April 20, 18 days later, the Sun has usually moved on into Taurus.

For the Chinese zodiac, Lunar New Year has always passed by April 2, so the animal is simply the one for the birth year. Well-known people born on April 2 include Hans Christian Andersen (1805), Émile Zola (1840) and Giacomo Casanova (1725).

faq.question: What zodiac sign is April 2?
faq.answer: April 2 is Aries in every year from 1930 to 2030, wherever you were born. It falls in the second decan of Aries, which tradition links with Sun.

faq.question: What is the Life Path number for someone born on April 2?
faq.answer: It depends on the birth year. On April 2 the Life Path is 4 in 1960, 5 in 1970, 6 in 1980, 7 in 1990, 8 in 2000, 9 in 2010 and 1 in 2020. The birthday number, from the day alone, is 2 for everyone born on the 2nd.

faq.question: What Chinese zodiac sign is someone born on April 2?
faq.answer: Chinese astrology is straightforward for an April 2 birthday: the new year began weeks earlier, so the birth year's own animal applies.

faq.question: Which famous people were born on April 2?
faq.answer: April 2 is also the birthday of Hans Christian Andersen (1805), Émile Zola (1840) and Giacomo Casanova (1725). The list comes from Wikidata and favours people with the most Wikipedia articles.
